_about: PARKED (Combat, 2026-10-23; docs/combat/biomes.md section 2). The signature's variant by the biome under the defender, one row a biome: its name, how its beam bites the terrain and structures, what it leaves behind, and its outcome flavour. It replaces the tables that hold this today: data/combat/templates.json beam.variants (the names), sim/world/crater.gd SCORCH_VARIANT (depth and width factors), the variant branches in sim/director/beam.gd sampleBeam (dust, sparks, fire), and beam.gd's unused copy const VARIANT (to delete on the switch). render/vfx/debris.gd also branches by the variant's name (glass flecks, spray puffs, larger embers); it keeps reading the name, which does not change. The seven rows marked asBuilt carry today's groove numbers and looks exactly, so with aftermathOn and byPersonality.enabled false, reading this file instead of the tables is bit-identical; only the new rows add behaviour. Game Design ruled both switches on (docs/design/rulings-2026-10-23b.md), so the table lands in two steps: first both off, then on. Biome keys are the names WorldBiomes.biomeAt returns; the eight new keys are provisional until World names its ids. Names are working labels until Legal screens them and Orb picks. The file picks what the beam carves, so it goes into DirData.dataHash as enders.json does.

fields.name: the label in the director's feed and the banner: upper case, place or material plus effect (Legal RL-008's pattern)
fields.scorch: [depth factor, width factor] on the groove (crater.gd: depth (D0 + D_P x P) x depth factor, half width (HW0 + HW_P x P) x width factor)
fields.areaMul: optional, 1 when missing: times the radius of the beam's structure damage (sampleBeam's damageArea) for the whole beam
fields.structMul: times the beam's structure bite (b.sf) for the whole beam. The variant is picked once, when the signature is planned, from the biome under the defender (as planBeam does today), and holds for the whole path
fields.trees: what the beam does to trees on its path: area (today's area damage), burn, fell (fall inward across the groove), snap (crowns drop), none
fields.fx: VFX's keys: dust colour, sparks, fire (sampleBeam's branches today; fire.withinAbove is in the prototype's units, times SimConst.WS as sampleBeam reads it); the other flags are new looks for VFX. Positions and counts stay in the code as today (one dust puff at g + 8 and the sparks at g + 6, inside the beam's reach test; one fire at g, under its own height test): the table carries only what varies
fields.aftermath: what the scar leaves for the rest of the fight (World's to build): null, or a kind from the aftermath table with its numbers. It is laid only on the groove's columns whose biome is the variant's own; where the beam carves on into another biome the groove there is plain
fields.outcomes: the flavour of each outcome here. Presentation unless the line starts with 'rule:', which marks a mechanical twist for Encounter and World

aftermath.clearing: the canopy over the groove is gone for the match: the strip no longer counts as forest cover, and the trees lie across it as fallen trunks (props a ricochet can plant on)
aftermath.fireLine: dry grass burns outward from the groove: spreads 1 column each spreadTicks for durTicks, up to reachCols each side; burns props and grass. With hazard, a fighter standing or sliding in it takes fire's hazard wear (living-destruction-numbers.md); flying over it costs nothing; it never finishes anyone, and hazard wear stays at most 15% of a match's wear (Game Design 23b item 5)
aftermath.heave: the groove's rim is thrown up as frozen plates rimMul x the berm: ground a slide stops against (World's WALL rule) and a slope a ricochet plants on
aftermath.snowDump: snow off the trees refills refill of the groove's depth over durTicks: a shallower scar under a powder curtain
aftermath.flood: the groove fills with water to the water table (wetland) or the sea (coast, where its floor is below sea level within seaCols of open water): a water trench under the ocean rules (sink, skim, submerge)
aftermath.scree: on a slope steeper than minSlope, rubble runs downhill from the groove up to reachCols over durTicks: a rubble strip (surface rubble: a slide over it tumbles)
aftermath.ember: the groove glows: its surface reads ember for durTicks, then crust; it lights props and grass. With hazard, a fighter standing or sliding on it while it glows takes fire's hazard wear, as fireLine; cooled to crust it is plain ground (Game Design 23b item 5)
aftermath.glaze: meltwater refreezes in the groove: its surface reads ice for the rest of the match (a slick strip)
aftermath.split: every floe the path crosses breaks at the path into two plates that drift gapBh apart: a lead of open water (a real gap in the ground)
aftermath.part: the sea parts along the groove for openTicks, an open trench walled by water; then the sea rushes back as a wave that pushes anything at the surface (fighters and props) pushBh along the beam's line (Game Design 23b items 8 and 10). Where the wave's line meets land within shoreCols, it runs up the shore: wet ground and props knocked over. The run-up is the same wave reaching land: it moves no fighter beyond the pushBh push and puts no one in water

ocean.name: HORIZON CLEAVE
ocean._rename: TIDE CLEAVE: Legal cleared it for adoption (RL-175; RL-006 found 'Horizon' a brand) and Game Design has no objection (23b item 8); it waits on Orb's pick
ocean._ruled: Game Design 23b items 8 and 10: the ocean's own aftermath settles ocean against plains; the sea parts for 1.5 s. The groove and looks stay today's, so the row is still asBuilt with aftermathOn false

_aftermathOn: ruled on (Game Design 23b items 5, 7, 8). Off, every row's name, groove and looks are read and nothing is left behind, which makes the seven built rows bit-identical with today: the first step of landing the table, before World builds the aftermath kinds

waterRule._ruled: Game Design 23b item 7 (and rulings-2026-10-19b.md 1e): a fighter dropped or landing in water by any row surfaces set within 30 ticks, with no down state beyond that, and counts as landed once he surfaces

_adoptProposed: true reads each row of proposed in place of the built row of the same biome. Left: the village's LANE SWEEP. Legal cleared it (RL-175) and Game Design ruled its collateral (23b item 9); it waits on Orb's pick (docs/combat/biomes.md section 2b). The ocean's row was ruled into variants (23b item 8)

village.name: LANE SWEEP
village._why: today the village plays the city's BOULEVARD RAZE exactly. Its own carve (signature-variants.md 5.3): a low, wide graze that scars along the lane, flattening a row of low houses a little each rather than gutting one. A wider structure radius at a lower bite. The name is Narrative's, cleared by Legal (RL-175)
village.collateral: the standing rules, no special case (Game Design 23b item 9): every person killed is on the firer's account, and the hero's own kills cost him (his cost meter, and 2 off Witness each); the tier's collateral budget caps the deaths, with no borrowing at tiers 1 and 2, so a row of houses over budget evacuates instead

personality._ruled: Game Design 23b item 9: near occupied houses the carer's graze narrows to 0.6 of its width and the villain's widens to 1.3, in place of byPersonality's widths for this row. The hero's LANE SWEEP takes the lane and spares more of the row

outcomes.CLASH: every roof along the lane lifts in a line, both ways from the meeting point
outcomes.GUARD: the guard is driven back down the lane, fences going flat ahead of him
outcomes.DODGE: the dodge vaults a roof ridge
outcomes.HIT: he is swept along the lane through the row of sheds
outcomes.ESCAPE: he breaks away low between the houses

byPersonality._about: signature-variants.md 5.1, ruled on by Game Design (23b item 6), inside every collateral budget: near people the carer narrows the bite and the one who feeds on collateral widens it. Off keeps every row as above (the first landing step)
